prs.title: fix: handle EPIPE and ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED in StdioServerTransport
prs.author: kai-agent-free
prs.reason: [llm pick] cluster primary for issue #1564: Both PRs change 3 files and both have unknown CI status, so neither wins on the top two criteria. The deciding factor is technical completeness: #1568 handles only EPIPE, while #1679 handles both EPIPE and ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED. These are two distinct Node.js stream errors that both occur when a client disconnects from a stdio server — EPIPE is emitted when writing to a closed pipe, and ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED is thrown when writing to an already-destroyed stream. Handling only EPIPE (as in #1568) leaves a real gap that would still crash the process under slightly different teardown ordering. With equal file counts, #1679's broader error coverage makes it the more complete fix for issue #1564 without being a larger or less focused diff.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs change 3 files and both have unknown CI status, so neither wins on the top two criteria. The deciding factor is technical completeness: #1568 handles only EPIPE, while #1679 handles both EPIPE and ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED. These are two distinct Node.js stream errors that both occur when a client disconnects from a stdio server — EPIPE is emitted when writing to a closed pipe, and ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED is thrown when writing to an already-destroyed stream. Handling only EPIPE (as in #1568) leaves a real gap that would still crash the process under slightly different teardown ordering. With equal file counts, #1679's broader error coverage makes it the more complete fix for issue #1564 without being a larger or less focused diff.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #1617 is backwards-compatible: it detects plain JSON Schema via isLikelyJsonSchema() and passes it through unchanged, preserving existing callers. It also fixes the type signature (ZodRawShapeCompat | AnySchema | undefined). PR #1596 takes the opposite approach — throwing an error on nested-object heuristic — which would break existing users and relies on a fragile signal that could misfire on valid ToolAnnotations with object-valued fields.
